summary.intent: Build a portal watcher/analysis agent for a hackathon (Soony supply-chain case), then work out how the agent can contact suppliers by email automatically, and finally add a one-off download command with documentation.
summary.outcome: The watcher was built and committed locally (2 commits, not pushed), a Nowak order email was drafted but not sent, and the mail setup was narrowed to a Gmail app password (after Cloudflare options were explored). An `ask-soony download [folder]` command with README and .env.example docs was added and tested, but not committed or pushed.

repo: The watcher is plain Python 3.14 with the anthropic and openai SDKs, SQLite, httpx and file-reading libraries. No agent framework is used; each backend has a ~60-line tool loop.
Portal files are stored by checksum in data/store/blobs/, which suits version history but is not browsable. A separate download command is needed to mirror them under original paths.
data/ is gitignored, so pushed commits contain no portal data. The team workflow requires git pull --rebase before pushing, and PROGRESS.md may conflict.
The agent's findings currently carry only a text 'suggested action'. A general act step (action proposal, approval, send and track) is still missing.
Mail should sit behind a small interface like the notifiers so SMTP/IMAP, Cloudflare or another provider can be swapped without touching the agent.
Planned mail safety rules: approval before sending, a recipient allowlist from supplier profiles, a rate limit, and a log of every sent mail.
The download command validates portal paths so nothing is written outside the target folder (a path-safety test was added).
workflow: The user requires asking before every git push; the assistant waited for approval despite the team workflow asking for an immediate push of the claim.

When unsure of facts about external services (Cloudflare pricing, subdomain routing, threading headers), the assistant checked the docs instead of guessing, and corrected itself when wrong (subdomain Email Routing does work alongside Private Email).
Sending to arbitrary addresses through Cloudflare Email Sending needs Workers Paid ($5/month minimum); receiving via Email Routing is free.
Cloudflare Email Routing on a subdomain works while the root domain keeps other MX records; the root only shows 'misconfigured', which is harmless.
Commits made through Entire's git hook are slow because the hook summarises the session; the author was set through env vars.

friction: No LLM key (Anthropic/OpenAI) or local model is available, so the agent with a real model remains untested.
The assistant gave inconsistent answers on Cloudflare (first said subdomain receiving was impossible, then set it up), and the user had to repeat a question about the $1 vs $5 plan.
Cloudflare sending returned 401 without Workers Paid, and the user decided against upgrading, which wasted the Cloudflare setup effort.
The user asked about the push status twice because the downloader commit was still local.
The path-safety test failed once and had to be fixed.
Mail options kept changing (Cloudflare, Private Email, IMAP, Gmail), delaying the build of the act step.
open_items: Push the 2 local commits (e532ff6, cdb7321) after git pull --rebase and a test run, once the user says 'push'.
Commit the new download command, README and .env.example changes, which are uncommitted.
Create the Gmail account with an app password, register it in the portal Settings and add the credentials to .env.
Build the act step: action proposals, an approval command (`ask-soony approve <id>`), SMTP send, IMAP inbox polling with thread matching, a supplier allowlist and an outbox log.
Add an LLM API key and run the first real agent test with `uv run ask-soony analyze --path suppliers/SUP-0028_Karton_Nowak/notices/`.
Decide whether to send the drafted Nowak order (the offer is valid 24 h from 2026-11-21) or let the product generate it.
Decide whether to remove the agents.stenglein.dev Email Routing DNS records, which were set up but are unused.
Set up a team-only Discord webhook and choose the deploy target (still open in PROGRESS.md).
Optionally switch to ASK_LLM_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5 to reduce analysis cost.
